bluf: WebFX is a US scaled performance agency founded in 1996 with 501-1,000 people, selling SEO, AI search visibility and measurement to mid-market buyers on the back of its RevenueCloudFX platform. The record shows a company moving its flagship search business onto the AI search line at full speed: GEO, ChatGPT optimization and ChatGPT ads pages, 86 AI search URLs in its sitemap, and LinkedIn ads that sell AI visibility to pipeline buyers. The one thing a rival should know: it practises what it sells on four of five tested lines, publishes plan pricing, and its book of 11 named clients carries no described work at all, so the proof behind the $10 billion revenue claim is the agency's own word.
doing:
WebFX describes itself as a tech-enabled, revenue-focused digital marketing agency and sells itself as a growth partner for the AI era, backed by RevenueCloudFX. In plain words: a high volume search shop that wraps every service in a measurement platform and claims the revenue it produces, over $10 billion in client revenue in the past five years by its own headline. The sold mix leads with SEO, AI Search / GEO and Data & Measurement, each scored 3. The SEO line is the flagship, with 1.3M+ page-one rankings claimed, a case library and plans with pricing. The AI search line has its own service pages for GEO, ChatGPT optimization and ChatGPT ads, and the homepage pitches visibility in search and AI. The measurement line is RevenueCloudFX attribution on the homepage plus MMM, channel attribution, call tracking and CDP services, with Customer360FX as the customer data platform.

Behind the leads sit Content & Digital PR (a Resource Furniture content case, copywriting and infographics, 40+ earned media wins claimed), Local (plans priced by location count, Record Head and PMI cases, review acceleration), Paid Search (a claimed 15% CPL cut in six months, the PaulB Parts case, enterprise PPC and LSA management), Paid Social and Web & Product (1,058 sites launched claimed). Fourteen of fifteen capabilities carry a score; AI Automation / Agents is the only zero. The proprietary set is RevenueCloudFX, Customer360FX, the SEO.com app (a DIY SEO tool launched 2024-04) and ELEVATE, a ChatGPT optimization process. The record lists one partner, Google Premier Partner, and WordPress as the CMS.

The AI posture is the revenue partner for the AI era: GEO and LLM SEO, ChatGPT optimization and ads, and AI visibility tracking inside RevenueCloudFX. Pricing is unusually public for its size: plan and pricing views for SEO, local SEO and web design, and advice to spend at least $5K a month on ChatGPT ads. Dated moves are thin and old: the SEO.com app launch in 2024-04 and Stevie awards in 2024 (Gold for the Customer360FX CDP, Silver for agency of the year). No news feed, case study dates or job postings were captured. Conspicuously absent for a company of its kind: any AI automation or agent line, any named enterprise platform partner beyond Google, and any listed office.
clients:
The record classes WebFX's clients as mid-market and lists ten verticals: home services, manufacturing and industrial, heavy equipment, retail and ecommerce, real estate and property management, legal, medical and health, finance and insurance, franchises, and tourism and hospitality. The home market is the United States; the record lists no offices.

Eleven clients are named, ten from case studies and one from a case study slug: Thompson Tractor, Kampgrounds of America (KOA), Resource Furniture, PaulB Parts, Marketview Liquor, Great Northern Corporation, HydroWorx, The Roof Detective, Property Management Inc. (PMI), Record Head and S. Clyde Weaver. None of the eleven carries a described engagement in the record, so every need is inferred from the sold mix rather than read from the evidence. The capability evidence does tie three of them to lines: Resource Furniture to the content marketing line, PaulB Parts to the PPC page, and Record Head and PMI to local SEO priced by location count. On that basis the observable needs are organic demand, paid performance, local and lead generation, and content, which is what a book of dealers, parts sellers, campgrounds, roofers and property managers buys. No client on this book appears on another tracked agency's book.

What the base needs next, as a judgment: these are lead-driven, multi location and industrial businesses whose search demand is being reshaped by KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and whose local demand is moving toward Business Profile and Local Services Ads work under KJ7. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that the next purchases across this book are AI visibility tracking tied to leads and calls, and LSA operation, both of which WebFX already sells. The weakness in the book is evidential: with 11 of 11 clients named only, a rival can ask any of them what the reported revenue actually was.
house: Four of five tested lines are practised on its own house and the integrity score is 80. It publishes llms.txt with 86 AI-topic URLs in its sitemap; it runs its own Google ads, 147 in the Transparency Center with 69 shown in the last 30 days (92 text, 29 image, 26 video, last shown 2026-09-27); it runs 24+ LinkedIn ads (22 company-page, 2 thought-leader), one of which reads "Driving pipeline starts with showing up everywhere your buyers search. Own your AI visibility"; and the sitemap shows 534 URLs updated in 90 days and 1045 in 365 out of 2145. The one contradiction is paid social: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site, which is also the Radar's one gap flag. The tag stack is GTM and VWO, so the CRO line has a testing tool behind it. No AI crawlers are blocked. Meta and TikTok ad libraries were not captured for any agency.
market:
The Horus read is Favored at +15.9, the 62nd percentile, with the sold mix at 17:12 on the Solar Arc (dusk). It is best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) through AI Search / GEO, and for KJ2 (ads inside AI answers) through AI search and paid search. It is most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) through SEO and paid search hours, and to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) through paid social and programmatic. Best scenario fit is The Walled Oasis at 40 and resilience 34.6. On the eight moves it is making four: an audited AI visibility product (P1), LSAs as core local work (P3), the inputs automation runs on (P4) and testing ads inside assistants with measurement (P8); partial on owned audiences (P7); absent on feeds and entities (P2) and on retraining juniors into agent operators (P6); pricing on outcomes (P5) is unknown to the record.

The Monsoon read is Onshore wind at 62.2, the 75th percentile: 56 of it is the sold mix, with SEO and web build carrying the most movable hours. Migration 55.7 against displacement 68.7, so the exposure runs through price competition on a mid-market, scaled performance book rather than through its own delivery moving. The shore split points 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. The read is inferred; the record lists no hub office, no hub hiring and no onshore claim.
openings:
The strongest opening is the unpixelled paid social line: WebFX sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site, so a rival that shows its own Meta and TikTok pixels firing and its own creative testing can, very likely, win the paid social conversation with a mid-market prospect comparing the two. The falsifier is a pixel appearing on webfx.com at the next Radar compile.

Second, the book buys on price: displacement 68.7 on the Monsoon read, published plan pricing for SEO, local SEO and web design, and a mid-market, scaled performance model. It is likely that an offshore-delivered or productised rival can undercut the SEO and local plans line by line; the counter is WebFX's own house, which practises what it sells and publishes 534 sitemap updates in 90 days.

Third, the evidence gap: 11 named clients with no described work. A rival pitching Thompson Tractor, KOA or PMI can lead with a request for the revenue proof behind RevenueCloudFX. Fourth, the machine-readable layer: no feed, schema or entity work in the record on a core search line, which is the P2 move the edition says answer engines consume; roughly even chance a schema and entity offer lands with the industrial and dealer clients. Low confidence on the last, because the record is silent rather than negative.
watch: Alphabet's Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, due late October 2026: below 10% flags cannibalization of the SEO line WebFX leads with, above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms the AI search pivot.
Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.
OpenAI ad run-rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the ChatGPT ads line WebFX advises $5K a month on lives or dies on the price of that inventory.
Holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing-model disclosures in October 2026: outcome pricing at a top-five holdco changes the KJ6 exposure of a scaled performance agency.
A social pixel on webfx.com, or a described engagement on any of the 11 named clients, at the next Radar compile.
